title: State Allocates $11.5 Million For Wilkinson Farm Industrial Park
description: The Harrodsburg Herald/Robert MooreFrom left: Judge-Executive Sarah Steele, U.S. Rep. Andy Barr, Mayor Bob Wil
content:
The Harrodsburg Herald /Robert Moore
From left: Judge-Executive Sarah Steele, U.S. Rep. Andy Barr, Mayor Bob Williams, State Rep. Kim King, State Sen. Amanda Mays-Bledsoe and Lt. Gov. Jacqueline Coleman took part in the check presentation ceremony on Monday, May 20.
The Harrodsburg Herald /Robert Moore
From left: Judge-Executive Sarah Steele, U.S. Rep. Andy Barr, Mayor Bob Williams, State Rep. Kim King, State Sen. Amanda Mays-Bledsoe and Lt. Gov. Jacqueline Coleman took part in the check presentation ceremony on Monday, May 20. Federal, state and local officials celebrated the allocation of $11.5 million in state funding for the development of the Wilkinson Farm Industrial Park. Officials attending the event included U.S. Rep. Andy Barr, Lt. Gov. Jacqueline Coleman, State Sen. Amanda Mays Bledsoe, State Rep. Kim King, Mercer County Judge-Executive Sarah Steele and Harrodsburg Mayor Bob Williams, as well as representatives from the Mercer County Fiscal Court, the Harrodsburg City Commission and the Harrodsburg-Mercer County Industrial Development Authority, among others.
The allocation is part of more than $21 million in state funding that will be invested in Mercer County thanks to appropriations made during the Kentucky General Assembly's recently concluded legislative session. The $11.5 million in funding for Fiscal Year 2025 comes from legislation that makes one-time investments towards paying down public pension liabilities, improving water infrastructure and preparing rural areas for economic development opportunities.
In addition, Greyson Evans, an economic development specialist with the Bluegrass Area Development District, announced the project would also receive federal funding in the form of a three-year U.S. Department of Transportation grant for planning and marketing.
'This is a true partnership,' Rep. Barr said Monday. 'This is a true collaboration.'
Last year, the fiscal court and the city commission voted to enter into a purchase agreement with Louisville Gas and Electric Company and Kentucky Utilities Company to purchase the 958-acre site. The primary focus is the development of a large-scale industrial factory that officials say could employ thousands. So far, the local stakeholders have invested more than $22 million in purchasing and planning for the site.
John Trisler, executive director of the industrial development authority and former county judge-executive, said officials have been in discussions to do something to spur local development for decades.
'I had gray hair—not white—when this started,' Trisler told the audience Monday. Trisler also announced they were close to signing a contract with American Engineers Inc. to create a master plan for the site, including infrastructure.
While some residents have criticized the purchase of the site and development of the industrial park, Trisler said it was vital for jobs and economic prosperity, 'not only for our community but for our region and our state.'

title: Stephan ‘Big Mac' Serrano, 12, Is An Ironman In Training
description: Photo Submitted
content:
Photo Submitted
Mercer County native Stephan Serrano pictured after eclipsing a sub 25 minute 5k last week in Danville. Mercer County resident Stephan Serrano has developed a talent for competitive running at the early age of 12, and since last summer, he has regularly challenged himself with runs across Kentucky. Serrano first began his running story in London, Kentucky, last year. Initially Serrano's mother, Mehgan Aguayo, took him to the race to see if he would enjoy it, but it soon developed into a passion for running and an inclination for America's most popular fast food chain. 'On the way back the only places that were open were McDonalds, so we stopped and he's like: ‘can I get a Big Mac?' So we got him a Big Mac, a large fry and a side of chicken nuggets and he devoured everything,' said Aguayo. Eventually, Serrano was in the mood for a Big Mac after all of his runs, so Aguayo began using McDonalds as positive reinforcement for achieving new goals on the course. 'We'd set goals and every time we would take a few seconds off, and he would hit it just so he could get a Big Mac,' joked Aguayo. Serrano doesn't frequent McDonalds, he was simply starving from pushing himself in his first competitive 5k. 'After I start running and I finish the race, I'm exhausted and empty, so I need something to fill me up and that's the main thing we go to,' said Serrano.

title: Two Killed In Boyle County Collision
description: The Kentucky State Police are investigating a vehicular collision in Boyle County that led to the death of both drivers. According to a KSP press release, the Richmond Post was contacted just before 5…
content:
The Kentucky State Police are investigating a vehicular collision in Boyle County that led to the death of both drivers. According to a KSP press release, the Richmond Post was contacted just before 5 p.m. ON Wednesday, May 29, about a two-vehicle collision on US-127 (Hustonville Road) near Bonta Lane in Boyle County. According to the KSP, a 2004 Black Chevrolet Blazer driven by David Wiegand, 49, of Mackville, was traveling north on US-127 and crossed the center line into the path of a 2004 Red Mazda, driven by Austin Wethington, 23, of Hustonville, who was traveling south. Wethington was fatally injured in the collision and pronounced deceased on scene by Boyle County Coroner Erin Guerrant, according to the KSP. Wiegand was transported to Ephraim McDowell Regional Medical Center, where he succumbed to his injuries and was pronounced dead. Trooper Clayton Cooper is conducting the ongoing collision investigation. He was assisted on the scene by Kentucky State Police personnel, Boyle County Sheriff's Office, Danville Police Department, Danville EMS, Boyle County Fire Department, and the Boyle County Coroner's Office.

sports@harrodsburgherald.com The Mercer County Senior High School track and field team has been hard at work this week in preparation for another strong showing at the KHSAA Class 2A state meet tomorrow, Friday, May 31, at the University of Kentucky track and field complex.
Several Titans are well accustomed to performing at the highest level of competition, and historically, Mercer County athletes tend to have the best performances of their season on the big stage. Over the last eight years, the Titans have opened the eyes of track and field fans across the state with their dominating performances at the state meet, but also with their depth and high level of competition in every event.
The Harrodsburg Herald /Samuel Warren

The Harrodsburg Herald /Samuel Warren
Senior Caden Semrau qualified for state with a shot put of 45 feet during the 5th Region meet in Harrodsburg last Tuesday, May 21. Among those upperclassmen, whose veteran mentality will lead the Titans into a fight for their fourth consecutive boys' state championship, are Kyler Sallee and Byron Collier.
Sallee has been an important piece of the Titan track and field squad for four years and has qualified for state in at least one event in each of those four years. Last season, Sallee competed in the 4×800, 4×400 and 4×200-meter relays, as well as the 300-meter hurdles. Sallee delivered a passionate and reassuring speech to the squad as they met following their first failure to win at least one 5th Region team championship since 2018.
'I guess what I was really trying to say was ‘just relax,'' said Sallee. The team leader, who has been a part of three straight state championships, had never experienced qualifying for state without already having a championship under his belt.
'My last three years, I've gone into the state championship an absolute nervous wreck; ‘can we win regions and state,' ‘what happens if we can't finish the job,' etc. It is different this time; with us coming up short in regions, there's nothing to lose and everything to gain,' said Sallee.
Collier will be competing in his third consecutive state championship meet and is searching for his first top-eight finish. Last year, Collier threw the discus more than 125 feet, but placed just fifteenth out of 22 competitors. This season, Collier has reached 140 feet on multiple occasions, and the University of Cumberlands track and field commitment won't dare let the big stage get in the way of his performance in the final meet of his high school career.
'I feel the most comfortable this year, having competed there two years before. I've realized I just have to treat it like any other meet, instead of being super nervous because it's a big meet, and I just have to go compete,' said Collier.
Mercer County fans attending the meet should keep their focus on several events where the Titan boys are likely to find success, including: the 4x800m relay, 110m hurdles, 300m hurdles 1600m run, 3200m run, 4x400m relay, shot put and discus, long, triple, and high jumps.
